naming_rules.wildcard_gt: matches one or more trailing tokens, last position only; never legal in the middle

areas.jobs: Compute job lifecycle events per queue: state, progress, log, dead-letter. Scheduler and workers publish; dashboard and data consumers subscribe.
areas.workers: Worker presence, capabilities, and state transitions at job-execution level.
areas.nodes: Mesh node presence and health at machine level (a node may run many workers).
areas.vault: PDM object lifecycle events (publish, supersede) that trigger or reference jobs.
areas.rpc: Request-reply services: submit, cancel, status, dequeue, stats. The caller publishes to the service subject with an _INBOX reply; the server subscribes to the service subject.
areas.internal: Instrumentation and ops: metrics feed for the dashboards, audit pointers, operator control.

kv.purpose: per-job scheduling state: priority, DAG refs, attempt, owner node

notes: Wildcards appear in SUBSCRIPTIONS only; publishers always emit fully specified subjects.
The job-id, worker-id, node-id, vault-id and queue segments are lowercase identifiers (a-z 0-9 - _); no wildcard characters in identifiers.
Queue segment values are the named lanes: default, priority, render, convert, gpu, and per-team lanes; fair-share and quota (P9-M2-T02) are enforced per queue stream consumer group.
Request-reply uses per-connection _INBOX.<token> reply subjects; the service subjects here stay concrete so a queue-group of handler instances can share them.
Reserved NATS system namespaces ($SYS, $JS, $KV, _INBOX.*) are never used as product subjects; the taxonomy lives entirely under the oep root.
